newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Jewish settler wounds two Arabs in West Bank.
newsitem.headline: Jewish settler wounds two Arabs in West Bank.

text.p: A Jewish settler shot and wounded at least two Palestinians during a stone-throwing incident in the West Bank on Monday, a settler spokesman said.

"As a result of massive stone-throwing on an Israeli car near the village of Kharbatha, the Israeli driver got out of his car and fired shots at the stone-throwers. Two Arabs were wounded, one seriously," the spokesman said. Officials at the Ramallah hospital said one Palestinian was wounded in the chest.

"It appears that two settlers were passing through the area and stones were thrown at them. They responded with gunfire. An incident ensued in which there was more shooting and a number of people were wounded. It is unclear how many," an Israeli security source said.
The West Bank and Gaza Strip have been rocked by daily unrest since Israel broke ground on March 18 for a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.
Three Palestinians have been killed by Israeli gunfire and scores wounded in the unrest.
The latest violence coincided with a crisis visit to the United States by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, due to meet President Bill Clinton later in the day.
